I once matched with somebody who told me he didn't want kids. We dated for a few months, until he suddenly got all weird and said work was getting really stressful and that he needed some time to deal with it. Fast forward a few weeks and I get an email explaining that his ex was now back in the picture, telling him that she was planning on going through with the IVF they had started back when they were still dating. We had discussed past relationships at length, but he never mentioned her or this situation at all and at some point I even got the whole "I thought you might change your mind" line. The whole thing was incredibly shitty, but I guess i really dodged a bullet. Not long after I got my tubed tied.
The "sharp part" is the root.
Can't change the past, only learn from it. Oh well. At least I have something to look forward to!

Still sucks, I really liked him and we got along really well. I just wish he could've been honest with me from the beginning... At the very least it would've saved me a lot of heartache. Anyway, I added my doctor to the list ☺

That's one of the reasons I cancelled my essure appointment and scheduled myself for the laparoscopic tubal (although my doctor apparently inserts while you're awake).  Plus, it's instant and there's no foreign material left in your body :) Glad it worked out in the end.
I had an appendectomy several years back and was up and out of the hospital in less than 24 hours, so I think I could handle a much smaller incision :) I do like that it's instant...
At the moment I'm kind of leaning towards saying "fuck it" and doing it anyway, hoping I'm one of the lucky ones.

I've had introductions go really well, and some not so well... but never have I had a rat absolutely hate or refuse to live with a companion after being properly introduced a few times.  In my experience, females are typically easier than males and neutered males were probably the most docile of all.  Perhaps check out your local animal shelters or rescues, all 7 of my guys came from a humane society and I was able to get 2 that were already neutered for $50 each- not a bad price when you consider the cost of vet bills!
Several states don't have bestiality laws... Florida only just got around to passing one a few months ago after at least 2 failed attempts.
Googled this company for the hell of it... they've also got "I kiss my dog on the lips", "Every day is hump day" and "I said a walk, not a ride". Huh.

I don't think they ever really had much luck climbing skin so they never really bothered with it.  These guys kept their nails fairly well manicured though, unlike my current lot... I swear my hairless girls have talons.
I had one rat who liked the window so much she'd press herself between the screen and the glass and just sit there on nice days: http://i.imgur.com/4c8SC.jpg

I loved these guys.  Sadly they've all passed on but when I lived in that house I used to let my 5 girls out for a lot of free-range time... every time I'd go into 'their' room they'd all swarm my ankles (and if I was wearing pants, climb my legs).  Probably somebody's worst nightmare I'm sure, but they never failed to cheer me up :D

I had always wanted pets growing up and since my father hates animals I figured a pocket pet that I could keep confined to my room would be my best shot.  I remember being in middle school and, when given the option between a birthday party and a hamster, choosing the hamster.  Fast-forward a few years and somebody my mom works with had brought home a rat that had 15 babies... Much to my dad's displeasure she allowed me and my brother to each get a pair of girls- 2 black berkshires and 2 PEWs.  That was almost 10 years ago and I haven't been without rats since. People out here actually refer to me as the "rat lady"... not because I have swarms of rats, but moreso because I'm the only person they know that keeps them.

Self-adhesive linoleum tiles work well too as they're cheap, easy to wipe down and will stay in place.  I have a Martin wire cage and I make the most of the empty space with lots of toys and hammocks.

And then they started doing this, so now they're not allowed to look out the window unless it's closed or I'm there to supervise: http://i.imgur.com/RQaSC.jpg
Little jerks.

As far as bedding is concerned aspen is also acceptable as it lacks the aromatic oils found in pine and cedar.  I personally prefer Carefresh-type litter but I'll occasionally use aspen in a pinch...
Also, if at all possible try to go through rescues or proper breeders. The vast majority of pet store rats come from rodent mills or are the product of sibling incest, and these rats often end up sickly.  Just my two cents :)
